review_output.summary: SCROLL_CIRCULAR drawing and the SCROLL/CIRCULAR CENTER/RIGHT-to-LEFT align override now use the cached label->text_size instead of measuring the current text at draw time, so the value goes stale whenever the text changes without going through lv_label_refr_text.
review_output.failure_scenario: A label uses lv_label_set_text_static(buf) in LV_LABEL_LONG_MODE_SCROLL_CIRCULAR. The app edits buf in place and calls lv_obj_invalidate(). draw_main still uses the old size.x, so the repeated copy is drawn at the wrong ofs_x (overlapping, or leaving a gap), and the 'size.x > width' checks that pick the alignment and decide whether to draw the circular copies give the wrong answer. The old code re-measured on every draw and handled this case correctly.

review_output.summary: The new public field lv_draw_label_dsc_t.text_size, documented only as 'The size of the text', is filled in by lv_label alone. Every other producer leaves it at {0,0} from lv_draw_label_dsc_init. Even lv_label fills it with a size wrapped at the pre-resize content width.
review_output.failure_scenario: The table (CELL_CTRL_TEXT_CROP), roller, textarea placeholder, scale, buttonmatrix, span and user lv_draw_label calls all pass text_size = {0,0}, some with LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND set. A custom or third-party draw unit, or a future change in lv_draw_label_iterate_characters, that reads dsc->text_size gets width 0. That would, for example, break alignment or line breaking. For a WRAP label, the field holds the wrapped size computed before lv_obj_refresh_self_size, not the size actually drawn.

review_output.summary: The new field is inserted in the middle of the public lv_draw_label_dsc_t (right after `text`), which shifts the offset of every later member and breaks ABI and positional initialization.
review_output.failure_scenario: Prebuilt draw units or libraries, MicroPython/other bindings generated against the old layout, and any positional/aggregate initializer of lv_draw_label_dsc_t now read font/color/etc. from the wrong offsets. The result is garbage fonts/colors or a crash dereferencing `font`. Appending the field at the end would avoid this.

review_output.summary: Altitude: the removed lv_text_get_size call was dead work to begin with. When LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND is set, lv_text_get_next_line returns early without using max_width (lv_text.c:336), so `w` never matters in this branch. The root-cause fix is to delete the measurement and use w = LV_COORD_MAX, not to add a cached size to a public draw descriptor.
review_output.failure_scenario: The PR adds a new public struct field, a new per-object field and state-sync code in lv_label_refr_text just to feed a value the callee ignores. That enlarges the API surface and the staleness risk (see findings 1 and 2) for no gain over a one-line removal that would also speed up table, roller and textarea draws.

review_output.summary: The NemaGFX backend keeps its own copy of the EXPAND branch and still calls lv_text_get_size(..., LV_COORD_MAX, ...) for every label draw, so the optimization is missing there and the two copies have diverged.
review_output.failure_scenario: On NemaGFX targets every EXPAND label draw still does a full-text measurement, so the performance fix has no effect there. The duplicated logic now differs from lv_draw_label_iterate_characters (dsc->text_size vs a recomputed size), which is a maintenance hazard.

review_output.summary: label->text_size duplicates the existing label->size_cache, which already caches lv_text_get_size for the same text, font and flags. The new field adds a second, differently computed cache that has to be kept in sync.
review_output.failure_scenario: Two caches of nearly the same quantity are refreshed at different times (text_size eagerly in refr_text, size_cache lazily in GET_SELF_SIZE with a different max width and a max_height clamp). Every lv_label instance also gets 8 more bytes, which adds up on RAM-constrained targets with many labels.

review_output.summary: In lv_label_refr_text the local `size` and `label->text_size` hold the same value. text_size is measured after lv_label_revert_dots but before the dots are applied and before lv_obj_refresh_self_size, so in DOTS/WRAP mode it describes neither the drawn text nor the final width.
review_output.failure_scenario: In DOTS mode, draw_main passes label_draw_dsc.text_size from the original un-truncated text, but the text actually drawn is the dotted one. If refresh_self_size changes the width, the measurement used the old max_w. Anyone who later relies on dsc->text_size for these modes gets the wrong dimensions.

review_output.summary: Adding 8 bytes to lv_draw_label_dsc_t grows every label draw task, because lv_draw_label and lv_draw_character lv_memcpy the whole descriptor into each task. Only one producer uses the field.
review_output.failure_scenario: Screens with many labels or characters allocate and copy extra bytes per draw task every frame on memory- and bandwidth-limited MCUs. Most of those tasks carry text_size = {0,0} because they don't come from lv_label.
